attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated as his own prediction.

semantics.note: The conditional 'if I'm right' and the implied antecedent of OpenAI's death are kept. 'Will' makes it a firm forecast if the antecedent holds. 'Most if not all', 'Anthropic included' and 'every investor' are preserved.

contract.note: Reading 'death' as business failure, 'most' as over half, and requiring a causal link are ordinary readings. No result turns on them yet because the antecedent has not occurred.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own dated announcement of ongoing business. It bears on the antecedent, which has not happened, not on the forecast outcome, so it cannot contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast whose antecedent, OpenAI's collapse, has not happened as of 2026-10-28. The evidence shows OpenAI still operating. Under the policy, a conditional whose antecedent has not occurred is not scored. No deadline was stated.

attribution.note: Zitron's own emphatic assertion in his post.

semantics.note: A universal causal claim ('every single stock') with the RAM/GPU-seller exception kept. The normalisation drops 'every single', but the contract restores it.

contract.note: A universal claim is fairly refuted by one well-documented counterexample. Palantir is clearly outside the hardware exception. Oracle's status is ambiguous, but the outcome does not depend on it.

evidence.note: Reuters, Aug 2025: Palantir shares jumped after a forecast raise driven by AI demand. Defense spending is also cited, but AI is a material documented driver.
A company disclosure of real AI product use. It corroborates the commercial substance but is not market attribution.
Independent same-day reporting ties Oracle's 36% jump to AI cloud revenue promises. Whether the exception covers Oracle is ambiguous.
Oracle's own disclosure of the backlog behind the market move. Company statement, not independent attribution.

reviews.rationale: The claim says every eligible stock's AI-attributed growth really comes from something else. Contemporaneous Reuters reporting ties Palantir's 2025 gains materially to AI demand, and Palantir is a software company outside the exception. Oracle's AI-driven jump is a further likely counterexample. Competing factors like defense spending do not remove AI's material role.

semantics.note: 'Will be obsolete' is a firm forecast. The horizon 'beginning of 2027' and the scope ('any and all' Blackwell and in-construction data centers) are kept.

contract.note: 'No longer commercially useful' matches the dictionary sense of obsolete, though it is stricter than 'superseded'. This will matter at the deadline, not now. Even the earliest reading of the deadline falls after the evaluation date.

evidence.note: NVIDIA says newer racks reuse existing cooling infrastructure. This is a company roadmap claim made before the deadline and does not settle the outcome.
Epoch reports Abilene operating at about 0.3 GW in April 2026. That predates the deadline and does not settle early-2027 usefulness.

reviews.rationale: The forecast's deadline, the beginning of 2027, falls after the 2026-10-28 evaluation date, and no conclusive event meets the early-resolution rule. Abilene was operating in 2026, which does not show its status at the deadline. Not scored yet.

attribution.note: The $2.8B figure is attributed to others ('allegedly'). The claim is Zitron's own belief that the burn was much higher.

semantics.note: 'I believe it burned much, much more' is a firm assertion about 2025, not a graded hedge. The separate funding figure is correctly left out.

contract.note: Reading 'burn' as net cash consumed is ordinary. The result depends on which cash measure counts. Requiring the same basis as the unreconciled estimate is strict but reasonable given that the speaker supplied no basis.

evidence.note: The audited S-1 shows a 2025 operating cash outflow of $2.637B and $131M of PP&E purchases, about $2.77B combined. This weighs against 'much, much more', but the metric differs, and the rest of the $3.08B investing outflow is unexplained.

reviews.rationale: The only usable evidence is GAAP operating cash flow from the audited S-1. Operating outflow plus capex is about $2.77B, which suggests no large excess over $2.8B. But it is a different metric from the cited estimate, and most of the investing outflow is not explained. The packet does not settle comparable cash burn.
